# grimoire-amix

> Developer- and LLM-oriented documentation for **Amiga Unix (Amix)** — Commodore's port of AT&T
> System V Release 4 (SVR4) to 68030 Amigas (A3000UX / A2500UX). It explains how Amix works, how to
> develop software and device drivers for it, and how to build custom boot/install disks with extra
> hardware drivers. Independent of, and cross-linked to, amigaunix.com; we go deeper on development.

The single source of truth (facts + citations + ✅/🟡/🔴 confidence tags) is
[research-brief.md](sources/research-brief.md). Contributor rules are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
For the full corpus in one file, see [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt).

## How Amix works
- [What Amix Is](docs/how-it-works/overview.md): SVR4/3B2 lineage, what it is and isn't, version timeline.
- [Supported Hardware & Requirements](docs/how-it-works/hardware.md): machines, MMU/FPU, the 16 MB ceiling, SCSI ID rules, Zorro II only.
- [The Amix RAM Ceiling](docs/how-it-works/ram-ceiling.md): the separate total-describable-RAM limit (~128 MB computed) — an unchecked rmalloc in page_init wild-writes from address 0, silently; detection fingerprint and per-rig RAM guidance.
- [Amix on 68040 and 68060 — Current Status](docs/how-it-works/68040-68060-status.md): why stock Amix is 030-only, what a port would require, what is being worked on, and what nobody should claim yet.
- [How Amix Boots](docs/how-it-works/boot-process.md): Superkickstart → bootblock → compressed kernel; RDB layout.
- [Kernel Architecture](docs/how-it-works/kernel-architecture.md): monolithic SVR4, /usr/sys, switch tables, MMU, STREAMS.
- [Filesystems & Disk Layout](docs/how-it-works/filesystems-and-disks.md): RDB partitions, UFS vs s5, /dev disk naming.
- [Networking](docs/how-it-works/networking.md): STREAMS TCP/IP, A2065, DNS-off default, NFS, SLIP.
- [X11 & the Desktop](docs/how-it-works/x11-and-desktop.md): X11R4/R5, OpenLook, A2410 color, RTG (X11R5 + X11R6.3 generations, Mesa 3.1).
- [Package Management](docs/how-it-works/package-management.md): the stock SVR4 pkg system — /var/sadm contents(4) DB, media formats, pkgadd mechanics, and a space-in-pathname defect that breaks pkgrm/pkginfo on the shipped image.
- [The Amix Package Repository Format](docs/how-it-works/package-repository.md): the static repo tree, the pipe-delimited catalog v1 grammar, md5+size integrity, the apkg client's three sources (HTTP / mounted medium / raw slice), and the fail-closed publish gates.
- [Quirks & Gotchas](docs/how-it-works/quirks.md): the Amiga-port surprises.
- [Z3660 board timings](docs/how-it-works/z3660-timings.md): CPLD clock rows are per-unit and per-clock — the laws, the 25.000 MHz edge, and the config-vs-failing-card diagnostic.
- [Emulation Fidelity](docs/how-it-works/emulation-fidelity.md): what a 68030/MMU/interrupt emulator must implement — format-$B bus-error frames, SCSI INT2 latency — or Amix's demand-paging boot fails, sometimes silently.
- [Glossary](docs/how-it-works/glossary.md): terms used across the docs.

## Getting started (emulation-first)
- [Running Amix in WinUAE](docs/getting-started/emulation-winuae.md): the exact config (MMU on, JIT off, SCSI 6/4).
- [Running Amix in FS-UAE](docs/getting-started/emulation-fs-uae.md): the verified FS-UAE config.
- [Amix on Amiberry](docs/getting-started/emulation-amiberry.md): Amiberry 8.x fully runs AND installs Amix — its A3000 on-board SCSI emulates the disk (ID 6) and tape (ID 4); plus real A2065 networking.
- [Putting Amix on your real LAN (Amiberry)](docs/getting-started/networking-on-the-lan.md): verified recipe — A2065 on a routed TAP + proxy-ARP; static IP, gateway, DNS, internet, reachable inbound, persistent at boot.
- [Installing Amix (Walkthrough)](docs/getting-started/install-walkthrough.md): boot+root+tape → partition → kernel → patch.
- [Running Amix on Real Hardware](docs/getting-started/real-hardware.md): A3000UX/A2500UX, modern SCSI.
- [First Login & a Quick Tour](docs/getting-started/first-login-and-tour.md): login, consoles, shells, X.

## Driver & software development
- [The Amix Device-Driver Model](docs/drivers/driver-model.md): major/minor, cdevsw/bdevsw switch tables.
- [Building & Installing a Kernel](docs/drivers/kernel-build.md): /usr/sys, kernel.c, make, make bootpart.
- [Composing Multi-Driver Kernels](docs/drivers/kernel-composition.md): why one kernel per root-storage family beats a universal all-drivers image — SDCARDS=2, the card-0 address sort vs the compiled-in rootdev, probe safety, the driver admission checklist, and the whole-kernel-package delivery path.
- [Reverse-engineering the prebuilt kernel](docs/drivers/kernel-reverse-engineering.md): disassembling the source-free /usr/sys/*/exp objects + reading globals from a savestate; worked on the mount(2)/vfssw fstype path (an errno-22 from `mount -F <fs>` = fstype not live in the booted kernel).
- [Writing a Character Driver](docs/drivers/writing-a-char-driver.md): the Ditto par.c walkthrough.
- [Writing a STREAMS/DLPI Driver](docs/drivers/writing-a-streams-driver.md): network drivers via hydra.
- [Zorro II AUTOCONFIG for Drivers](docs/drivers/zorro-autoconfig.md): autocon(), board IDs, /dev/mem scanning.
- [X11 RTG Graphics Drivers](docs/drivers/x11-rtg-drivers.md): an X server over a kernel framebuffer driver — two generations: Xrtg/VA2000 (X11R5) and Xzz9000/ZZ9000 (X11R6.3).
- [Toolchain & Packaging](docs/drivers/toolchain.md): native cc/gcc + the gcc-cross-amix Linux cross-toolchain (m68k-cbm-sysv4), elf2brel, pkgadd.
- [Case Study: va2000-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/va2000.md): char framebuffer driver (MNT VA2000).
- [Case Study: xrtg-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/xrtg.md): X11R5 server for the VA2000.
- [Case Study: lszorro-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/lszorro.md): userspace Zorro II scanner.
- [Case Study: hydra-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/hydra.md): STREAMS/DLPI Ethernet driver.
- [Case Study: zz9000-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/zz9000.md): kernel framebuffer driver for the MNT ZZ9000 (Zorro II product 3; /dev/zz9000 char major 49) — mode setting, mmap, ioctl API, late-activated ANSI framebuffer console; the foundation of the X11R6.3 RTG stack.
- [Case Study: x11r6.3-amix (Xzz9000)](docs/drivers/case-studies/x11r63-zz9000.md): an X11R6.3 port whose Xzz9000 server drives /dev/zz9000 through a card-generic RTG DDX layer; documents the native Amix shared-library ABI (ld -G -h runtime images + .sa stub archives, strict link order).
- [Case Study: mesa-amix (Mesa 3.1)](docs/drivers/case-studies/mesa31.md): OpenGL on Amix — Mesa 3.1 software rendering via the Xlib driver against Xzz9000; static libGL/GLU/glut bootstrap, no server-side GLX.
- [Case Study: A4091 / 53C710 SCSI driver](docs/drivers/a4091-53c710-driver.md): booting Amix from a Zorro III A4091 — the 68030 TT-gap obstacle, sptalloc, the 53C710 SCRIPTS driver, and chipset-gated auto-detection (emulation-proven).
- [Case Study: Z3660 ethernet driver (zen0)](docs/drivers/z3660-ethernet-driver.md): native SVR4 STREAMS/DLPI driver for the Z3660 accelerator's onboard Zynq ethernet — the firmware frame-mailbox protocol, polled RX (no int2_tbl), the INT6 interrupt-storm fix; full bidirectional TCP/IP on real hardware (A4000 + Z3660, 2026-06).
- [Case Study: Z3660 piscsi SCSI driver (z3660.c)](docs/drivers/z3660-scsi-driver.md): the Z3660's onboard "SCSI" is not a SCSI chip but the PiStorm piscsi register mailbox ported to its Zynq ARM — a ~5-poke synchronous block driver, the multi-method detect that cleared a silent hang, and the firmware-emulator bug that masqueraded as a driver hang; booted Amix multiuser with root on real hardware (A4000 + Z3660, 2026-06), first try.

## Custom boot & install disks
- [Anatomy of the Boot Floppy](docs/boot-disks/anatomy-boot-adf.md): bootblock + compressed kernel.
- [Anatomy of the Root (miniroot) Floppy](docs/boot-disks/anatomy-root-adf.md): UFS installer + scripts.
- [Anatomy of the Patch Floppy](docs/boot-disks/anatomy-patch-adf.md): self-extracting sh + cpio.
- [Reverse-Engineering the Boot Floppy](docs/boot-disks/reverse-engineering-boot-adf.md): the kernel is Unix compress/LZW → m68k ELF; the checksum is non-fatal; how to extract and rebuild.
- [Adding Drivers to a Custom Boot Disk](docs/boot-disks/adding-drivers-to-boot-disk.md): three delivery surfaces (boot partition, bootable floppy, add-on disk).
- [The Boot-Disk Tooling Pipeline](docs/boot-disks/build-pipeline.md): inspect / extract-kernel / build-bootfloppy / unpack / build scripts.
